scope: Read-only review of all 12 requirements and 26 cases, canonical research/spec pages, all 51 exact retained native records, original chunk lines and code hashes, 10 manifest payloads, H4/N5 copies and finite arithmetic. Not a handoff release review.

findings.location: wiki/specs/bundled-device-hosting.md: scope; REQ-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING-001/002/004/005/006/007; BDH-001 to 006 and 010 to 014
findings.problem: The S labels are justified as static observations of a recovered internal host-to-bundle path, but these cases assert Prepared channels/flags, pending-control order and delivery count, partition-local event coordinates, subrange transport context and clearing of one internal queue. The draft makes their application-observable effect U and supplies no established external observation point for those intermediate values. Renaming them logical inputs/outputs and allowing alternative partitions does not make their intermediate delivery observable: passing these cases would still require reproducing or instrumenting an analyst-selected component decomposition. In particular A4 gives the internal flush boundary as an input, not an independently observable UI/automation interval. A candidate producing the same app audio/files/UI through different control coalescing, event partitioning or event re-creation must not fail solely for a different internal trace.
evidence: REQ-004 and BDH-010/011 require final updates in first-arrival order, once each, then empty delivery; the source records 45/32 prove that implementation queue, not that the order/count is externally distinguishable.

REQ-005/006 and BDH-012/013 observe subblock events/context; real timestamp origin and scheduler context units remain U under A2/A3 and REQ-012. Source record 15 proves the internal transform for the constrained vector, not a candidate-visible event timeline.

REQ-007 and BDH-014 isolate clearing one event queue; the requirement expressly leaves upstream note re-creation, voice continuity and audio output U. Source records 31/44 support queue clearing, but the app-level result cannot be graded from absence in that specific original queue.

REQ-001/002 and BDH-001 to 006 observe buffers/presence supplied to a private wet operation. Their signal-preparation finding is useful; presence/activity observability and a composed device-output comparator are not established by the copy/zero code alone.
findings.requested_change: Preserve these S facts and finite derivations in canonical research, and explicitly classify the intermediate cases as non-normative analysis/component model checks excluded from application compatibility/covered-requirement counts. Retain corresponding application audio/behavior requirements as U unless a public or otherwise independently established external input/output boundary and observable comparator can be supplied. Do not require the candidate to expose this ABI, partition, queue or processing interface. This is a classification correction, not a request to discard source findings or run prohibited original/emulated execution. Update spec/packet/case-index/coverage counts and snapshots consistently.

findings.problem: The settled DryWet algebra is directly supported and its finite arithmetic is correct. It is a useful conditional composition law with wet output supplied as an explicit dependency, but the three synthetic wet values are analyst vectors, not captured Amp/Cabinet output. They must not be counted as full-device or application-audio closure.
findings.requested_change: When resolving finding 001, retain the steady output law as conditional static composition if desired, and distinguish its analyst arithmetic vectors from any eventual app/device audio acceptance case. Preserve unsupported transitions, wet DSP, path-selection/scheduling and whole-app output as U.

static_findings_supported.subject: Stereo and mono preparation
static_findings_supported.result: Selected effect path copies both channels when present or zeroes both; dual-mono paths preserve independent wet inputs; mono wet input is (L+R)/2, while original dry stereo reaches the mixing operation. Source observation only; external composition classification finding above.

static_findings_supported.subject: Steady host mixing
static_findings_supported.result: Steady sin(d*pi/2) wet and sqrt(1-wet^2) dry laws match the code and BDH-007 to 009 finite calculations. Sample rounding and transition law remain outside these comparators.

static_findings_supported.subject: Parameter coalescing
static_findings_supported.result: Last value replaces a repeated pending index; first-seen order retained; delivery clears queue. Count guard precedes lookup at full capacity. A4 excludes grouped path and capacity edge, matching the source. This remains an internal transform, not an application observation.

static_findings_supported.subject: Event filtering/rebasing
static_findings_supported.result: Filter permits types 1/2/6 and type 3 codes -2,-1,1,64,74,120. Queue cap 4,096; local split cap 2,048. Ordered vector coordinates 0/511/512/1023 map to [0,511] in each half-open 512-frame region. Residual frames and origin remain U; record 15 stack recovery warning preserved.

static_findings_supported.subject: Transport advancement
static_findings_supported.result: Nonlooping split arithmetic adds tempo*start/(rate*60) while playing and zero while stopped. BDH-013 increment 8/375 at 120 BPM, 512 frames, 48,000 Hz is correct. Numeric producer semantics and loop-boundary law remain U.

static_findings_supported.subject: Rate notification and reset
static_findings_supported.result: Ordinary Reset and NewRate have no calls to host warm-up helper 0x102fbff98. NewRate updates stored rates, invokes rate/reset, restores cached index 0 for reset-capable primary, clears the queued-event count and restores prior readiness. ResetAndDispatch calls helper exactly four times, first with one event then three without; helper requests 1,024 frames each. With the 512-frame capability this is 4,096 total warm-up frames on that path. No claim about when insertion selects it or audible reset/tails is established.

static_findings_supported.subject: Activity and resource release
static_findings_supported.result: Activity/success are separate; activity/input, queued/control change, prior state, fades, readiness and smoothing affect processing. Record 39 return type conflicts with caller consumption; record 43 warnings remain. Exact stop/restart is correctly U. Exit unregisters callbacks; destructor releases extant instances, decrements loader count, and on zero releases bundle through cleanup. This is resource-mechanism evidence, not a user deletion/cancel/tail guarantee.
